speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: First, is to apply the maximum tax relief period for each Pioneer Certificate (PC) on the incentivised activities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The Pioneer Incentive is designed to attract and anchor new economic activities, that is, pioneer activities with significant economic benefits to Singapore and to encourage companies to acquire new technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The objective of the incentive is to drive the growth of high value-added or high-technology industries in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Clauses 3, 4 and 13 amend sections 5, 6 and 17 respectively to give legislative effect to this.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The second major change is to apply the maximum tax relief period for each certificate issued for Development and Expansion Incentive (DEI) on the incentivised activities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: DEI was introduced to encourage companies to expand by investing in technology as well as major upgrading of equipment and operations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Under the EEIA, the tax relief period under DEI is generally capped at 20 years and currently applied on the company, instead of the incentivised qualifying activities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Therefore, clauses 17 and 18 amend sections 19J and 19K respectively to give legislative effect to this.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The remaining legislative changes arising from our periodic review of the income tax system are technical in nature or relate to improvements in tax administration.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: These changes also reflect the Government's commitment to monitor the effectiveness of our tax incentive regime and to keep it competitive and relevant as economic conditions change.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, I would like to seek some brief clarifications and also make some suggestions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are amendments to section 17 of the Act but not to section 17(2) specifically, which states "The Minister may, if he considers it expedient in the public interest to do so, approve the application and issue the company with a certificate subject to such terms and conditions as he thinks fit".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister also consider this for section 4(1) which states "The Minister may, if he considers it expedient in the public interest to do so, approve an industry, which is not being carried on in Singapore on such a scale adequate to the economic needs of Singapore and for which in his opinion there are favourable prospects for development, to be a pioneer industry and any specific product of that industry to be a pioneer product." EDB does have some of this information on its website and factors of consideration as well, but I hope we can provide more clarity in the legislation itself.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need a clear and unambiguous framework to select and admit companies which will benefit from the pioneer status.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I ask this so that companies can also better understand the considerations taken and, hence, can plan accordingly and make better plans to become pioneer industries or pioneer service companies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This greater clarity will again allow companies to make better plans which will, ultimately, benefit Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The main aim of providing all these clarifications is so that companies have a higher chance of a successful application, resulting in fewer resources wasted through failed and repeated applications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second concern is how we can help more SMEs and startups benefit from these tax reliefs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: SPRING Singapore is already helping the start-ups with the ACE Start-ups Grant and all companies, especially the SMEs, with the Productivity and Innovation Credit Scheme.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will EDB be doing more to help them also become pioneer industries and pioneer service companies?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It does seem like a huge hurdle to overcome to become a pioneer industry and I hope we are not setting a hurdle too high for SMEs which, with a bit of help, have the potential to be global game changers and make Singapore proud.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, many companies are aware of the PIC scheme but far fewer are aware of the Economic Expansion Incentives Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope we can roll out more initiatives to increase awareness and encourage more applications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will be in line with our overall goal of building up innovation, inspiring more creativity and driving more research and development in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I believe that with more clarity on the criteria for the approval of applications, more awareness and, with the amendments proposed in this Bill, our efforts will be further strengthened.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Mr Ng has suggested that we provide more clarity on the qualifying criteria for the Pioneer Certificate (PC) as well as the Development and Expansion Incentive (DEI) so as to raise companies' awareness of the incentive under the Act.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: But at the same time, we also have to be flexible and responsive to the complexities and special needs of the different economic sectors as we have to deal with a very complex economic environment.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: The objective really is to encourage "queen bees" to set up operations here and thereby help build a cluster around them.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Applications are, therefore, assessed based on the scale and the qualitative aspect of their economic contributions to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: The exact level of support is thereafter calibrated to commensurate with the level of economic contributions from the company.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: The actual incentive awarded to the company will depend on the combination of these factors.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: And over time, in fact, they have also raised the bar and the requirements for the various criteria to ensure that only deserving companies receive the incentives.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: EDB keeps companies informed of the PC and DEI schemes through regular engagements and companies interested to apply for these schemes are, of course, welcome to approach the EDB for further details.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Mr Ng also asked how SMEs and startups can benefit from these schemes, especially those with the potential to become globally competitive.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: As Members can well understand, PC requires companies to commit to economic contributions of substantive scale and, therefore, it is quite natural that the bigger companies will tend to qualify.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Although the PC and DEI may not be the suitable platforms to develop our SMEs and start-ups, I would like to assure Members and Mr Ng that the Government agencies have a range of programmes in place to support the different needs of companies along their various stages of growth.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: For example, SPRING Singapore partners incubators to support innovative startups to scale up.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: SPRING also supports SMEs to innovate and raise productivity through schemes, such as the Capability Development Grant.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: IE Singapore helps our companies on their internationalisation efforts and EBD works closely with our local enterprises to develop our economic and various industry clusters, including partnering SMEs on capability transfer and supplier development through initiatives, such as Partnerships for Capability Transformation (PACT).

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: The Government will continue to review our incentives on a regular basis to ensure that they remain relevant and meet the needs of the different types of companies that we have.      .
